disease_name.evidence: Huanglongbing (HLB) is a major disease of citrus that has caused catastrophic damage to citrus trees worldwide.

pathogen_scientific_name.evidence: The pathogen currently found in the US is Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus.

affected_parts.evidence: yellow shoots with pale green and yellow flushes. non-symmetrical mottled leaves... thickened, leathery leaves... enlarged, corky mid-ribs of leaves... Defoliation, fruit drop, and shoot dieback occurs in more advanced stages... The vascular tissue is brownish at the peduncle side of fruit... Maintaining trees in good health, especially root health, is important

summary.value: Huanglongbing causes reduced fruit quality and yield, tree decline, and eventual tree death, with symptoms including yellow shoots, mottled leaves with shades of yellow and green, thickened leathery leaves, and eventually defoliation and shoot dieback.
summary.evidence: Huanglongbing (HLB) is a major disease of citrus that has caused catastrophic damage to citrus trees worldwide. The disease causes reduced fruit quality and yield, tree decline, and eventual tree death. Typical symptoms include: yellow shoots with pale green and yellow flushes. non-symmetrical mottled leaves (shades of yellow and green on either side of the mid-rib).

diagnostic_features.value: Non-symmetrical mottled leaves with color gradients on either side of the midrib, thickened and leathery leaves with enlarged corky midribs, fruit that are small, lopsided, and asymmetrical with color inversion from yellow/orange on peduncle side to green on stylar end, brownish vascular tissue in fruit, and small brown aborted seeds.
diagnostic_features.evidence: non-symmetrical mottled leaves (shades of yellow and green on either side of the mid-rib). thickened, leathery leaves. enlarged, corky mid-ribs of leaves... small, misshaped fruit that are lopsided or asymmetrical and exhibit color inversion from yellow to orange to green on the peduncle side while remaining green on the stylar end. The vascular tissue is brownish at the peduncle side of fruit. Seeds of affected fruit are small, brown, and aborted.

look_alikes.evidence: The lab can also test for citrus stubborn, which can have similar symptoms in the foliage of infected trees.

type_of_disease.evidence: The rotted portion of the fruit was covered with a white, compact fungal growth with olive green spores.

summary.value: Orange fruits develop rotting covered with white, compact fungal growth and olive green spores; some fruits become shriveled and mummified.
summary.evidence: The rotted portion of the fruit was covered with a white, compact fungal growth with olive green spores. Some fruit were shriveled and mummified.

diagnostic_features.value: White, compact fungal growth with olive green spores; dense olive green colonies 18-22 mm diameter with coremia (fungal fruiting structures); conidia mostly cylindrical or obpyriform.
diagnostic_features.evidence: The rotted portion of the fruit was covered with a white, compact fungal growth with olive green spores. Dense and olive green colonies 18 to 22 mm in diameter appeared on CYA media having coremia. Conidia were mostly cylindrical or obpyriform.
